source.question: F-12's water cut fell from about 0.97 to about 0.3 at the end of 2014. What was done to the well, and why did the plug set in 2010 not do the same?

note: Reviewed Oct 28 night: fair (values and dates from evidence not cited, 'cause' in a fact, an unhedged 'caused'). Its detail's 'water 0.3107 to 0.7745' was also read as water, not the water cut: fixed (tool-speak 'water' on a value the evidence holds only as a water cut).

submission.summary: Re-checked: the 2010 water-cut jump flagged for 2010-10-24 is a gradual rise averaged over long periods, not an abrupt +0.30 step caused by the plug — daily rates stay near 0.61 to 0.68 through the work and BHP zero is a gauge fault with the well still flowing. The late-2014 drop to about 0.31 is tied to F-12-specific work at 3,150 m plus new perforations, not a field-wide shut-in flush — liquid rate and choke both fell sharply at that time while field injection kept pace, and the gain persisted through 2015 on a steady decline rather than a transient peak.

findings.claim: The 2010 plug at 3,210 m did not cause an abrupt water worsening; the 0.513 -> 0.814 shift flagged around 2010-10-24 is a long-window average change, not a step at the job.
findings.detail: Detect_events regime 2010-10-24 compares months before (mean 0.513 from 2010-02-14) to months after (mean 0.814 to 2016-08-14). Daily data 2010-09-24 to 2010-09-27 water_cut 0.61-0.60 and 2010-10-11 0.664 to 2010-10-24 0.676 shows no +0.30 jump after the 2010-09-20 to 2010-09-23 workover. Production_log low rate: below 3210 m oil 0.011 water 0.325 so plug removed only ~32% of water.

findings.claim: From 2010-10-12 BHP reads zero while the well keeps flowing, confirming a sensor failure not a pressure event linked to water rise.
findings.detail: BHP last good 253.9 bar on 2010-10-11, then null on 2010-10-12 onward while oil 1759 Sm3/d that day and 1665 Sm3/d on 2010-10-24; gauge_failure event notes 2095 zero days with 1830 flowing days and 1,133,053 Sm3 oil during failure window.

findings.claim: F-12's water cut fell from about 0.96 to about 0.31 after isolation at 3,150 m and new perforations at 3,126 to 3,140 m.
findings.detail: Monthly 2014-11 0.9623 to 2015-01 0.3107 across 32-day shut-in 2014-11-30; workover 2014-11-26 installed plug at 3150 m and perforated 3126.2-3139.7 mMD while PLT below 3150 showed 97.1% of water entered there.

findings.claim: The 2014 change is not just a field-wide shut-in or choke effect; F-12's liquid and choke both dropped sharply at the workover while field injection stayed balanced.
findings.detail: Waterflood monthly liquid 4923 Sm3/d in 2014-11 to 1251 in 2015-01, choke 100% to 30.28%, year 2014 to 2015 liquid 5106 to 1583 Sm3/d; field voidage replacement 1.02 in 2014 and 0.9995 in 2015 shows injection kept pace, not a voidage drop. Well-specific plug+perforation coincides with 2014-11-22 to 2014-11-27 job.

findings.claim: The oil gain persisted through 2015 at a moderate decline, not a transient post-shut-in flush, reaching about 0.77 water cut by year-end.
findings.detail: Exponential decline 2015-01-02 to 2015-12-31 qi 880.46 Sm3/d, di 0.9598 per year, r2_log 0.8764, no warnings; monthly oil rate 862.38 in 2015-01 still 356.26 in 2015-12, water 0.3107 to 0.7745; longer window to 2016-08 qi 928.15 di 1.17 r2_log 0.9522.

surveys.read_from: LAS files of the interpreted log (Well_logs_pr_WELL/15_9-F-12/10.PRODUCTION LOGS/PLT Sept 2010)

result.note: A production log measures the flow passing each depth while the well flows; going up, it grows past each zone that produces. A share at a depth is the part of the pass's oil or water entering below that depth (1 at the bottom of the well's inflow, 0 above the top zone). comes_in_from_m to to_m holds 90% of each phase's inflow. Only shares are given: the files' rates have no units, and the plots' are downhole volumes. A plug set at a depth shuts off what enters below it: the shares below say what it could remove. Each survey's passes were run at several surface rates. A survey read off pictures carries the checks of that reading.

result.no_trend: WOR is not rising with cumulative oil on 2013-05 to 2016-08: no limit can be projected
result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.

arguments.sql: SELECT date, well, oil_sm3, water_sm3, water_cut, choke_pct, bhp_bar FROM production_daily WHERE well='F-12' AND date BETWEEN '2010-09-20' AND '2010-11-30' ORDER BY date LIMIT 80
